solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The French: not crazy about good pasta

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

indicators.note: the word for 'not crazy' is placed around the letter for 'good'

parts.note: someone not crazy is sane

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark that the French are not keen on a decent plate of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a type of flat, wide pasta, also the baked dish made with it.

clue.text: Ring certainly being snatched by hooligan — take care!

indicators.note: the letters for ring and certainly are seized and held within the word for hooligan

parts.note: a lout is a yobbish, rowdy man
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
OK means yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A warning to take care when a hooligan grabs a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'look out!' is a warning to be careful, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Attractive selection of pieces on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word for a set of pieces is given as it is spoken

parts.note: a suite is a set of musical pieces played together

explanation.surface: A pleasant medley of music played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes something charming or cute, a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Substance not entirely used on second machine

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for substance loses its final letter

parts.note: the gist is the substance or essence of something
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A material only partly used in a second machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is a gadget or small device, informally a contraption or machine.

clue.text: Magazine finally fast to secure this writer as contributor?

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Magazine
the word for fast is fastened round the setter's pronoun

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
this writer is the setter, so me

explanation.surface: A magazine at last makes a quick deal to get this writer as a contributor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quickly'; it is the season of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component part, something that contributes to a whole.

clue.text: Looking horrified at Society backing criminal group

indicators.note: backing means the words at and Society, as letters, are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is a gang of criminals, such as a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at a society that supports a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' looks like part of the definition, but it joins Society inside the 'backing' reversal, making STA.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare is to gaze wide-eyed, as one does in shock or horror.

clue.text: Not generally the emotion of a blue movie?

definitions.text: Not generally the emotion of a blue movie?

parts.words: Not generally the emotion of a blue movie?
parts.note: blue can mean pornographic or unhappy; a blue film in the first sense is rarely about the second

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests an adult film, but the feeling of being blue is gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling low, so this emotion is melancholy or sorrow.

clue.text: Make sure it's a crane that's taken apart

indicators.note: something taken apart is dismantled and can be put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Checking that the crane on site has really been dismantled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, establishing a fact beyond doubt.

clue.text: Taxmen assessed about it getting annoyed

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

indicators.note: the word for assessed goes around it

parts.note: rated means assessed or valued

explanation.surface: Tax inspectors evaluating something and getting cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue merged into HMRC in 2005, so the abbreviation is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated is a synonym for annoyed: provoked and impatient.

clue.text: Live with damage found on Greek language textbook

indicators.note: in a down clue, found on means the later pieces sit below the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: I am means I exist or live
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A battered Greek textbook bearing the motto 'live with damage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar is a book setting out the rules of a language's structure.

clue.text: Run out of cash? Deliveries are kept on hold

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so deliveries come in overs
to pend is to remain undecided or awaiting settlement

explanation.surface: Someone short of money whose parcels are held up in transit.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is a set of six balls, each called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more than you have is a playful way of saying you run your money dry.

clue.text: Military boss advanced to seize head of regiment roughly

indicators.note: the commander's letters take hold of the first letter of regiment, enclosing it

parts.note: CIC stands for Commander-in-Chief

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of regiment is taken

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A senior officer who moved forward to take command of a regiment, approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is a Latin preposition meaning approximately, used before dates.

clue.text: University book including chapter giving result

parts.note: OU is the Open University

indicators.note: the word for book takes the letter for chapter inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A university textbook with a chapter that reveals a result.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of something; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Slip — or its content?

definitions.meaning: a slip here is a mistake, especially a printing error
a slip of paper inserted in a book carries the correction of a printing mistake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' does double duty: the mistake itself and the paper slip on which publishers list it.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing, listed on an inserted correction slip.

clue.text: Revenue collectors? Everyone upset about Government filling bags!

indicators.note: the inner group of letters goes inside the word for bags

parts.note: totes are bags, as in tote bags

indicators.note: the reversed word for everyone goes around the letter for Government
upset in a down-the-page sense means the word for everyone is turned backwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A protest that everyone is angry at the Government stuffing its bags with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL into LLA, and 'about' puts it round G to give LLGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barriers on toll roads take payments, so they literally collect revenue.

clue.text: Sign of age in meat — best to be returned

parts.note: liver is an organ meat sold by butchers

indicators.note: returned means the word for best is sent back, read upward in this down clue

parts.note: the tops means the best

explanation.surface: Meat that is past its best being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver spots are brown skin blemishes typical of older people, so a mark of ageing.

clue.text: Grand poet, struggling, finds sponsor

indicators.note: struggling means the letters are in disarray and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A great poet in difficulties finds a patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like G, but the whole word joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: At baptism a godparent stands as sponsor, vouching for the child's upbringing in faith.

clue.text: Person on boards tense, blocking a company's source of recovery

indicators.note: the letter for tense sits in the middle of the word for company, blocking it

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of recovery is taken

explanation.surface: A tense board member stands in the way of a firm's financial recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' suggests a company board; here it is the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards means acting on stage, so a performer there is a thespian.

clue.text: Went wild — greatly desired to keep volume up

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the letter for volume inside it
up tells the solver to turn the word for greatly desired backwards

parts.note: something dear is much loved or desired

explanation.surface: Someone who lost control, longing to turn the volume up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DEAR to RAED, which 'to keep' wraps round V.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk wildly or rage incoherently, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Result of declining to create cut in curtailed area

indicators.note: in means the shortened word for create sits within the shortened word for area
curtailed means the last letter of the word for area is cut off

parts.note: a realm is a domain or area

indicators.note: cut means the word for create loses its last letter

parts.note: to create is to make a fuss

explanation.surface: A refusal to make cuts in a reduced area of spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'create' is used in its informal British sense of 'kick up a fuss'. 'curtailed' makes REAL, 'cut' makes FUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining an offer produces a no, so the noun is what declining yields.

clue.text: Always disputing description of singular downpour?

definitions.meaning: describes a life of constant quarrelling, like a married couple fighting
heavy rain is said to come down in cats and dogs; made singular, the phrase loses its plural endings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raining cats and dogs' is an idiom for a downpour; take the singular nouns for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-and-dog life is one of perpetual bickering, like the animals' supposed enmity.

clue.text: Angler's action almost catching American snappers

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the abbreviation for American, as a line catches a fish
almost means the last letter of the word for an angler's action is dropped

parts.note: an angler casts a line
Amer is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A fisherman almost lands some American snapper fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Snappers are fish, but here things that take snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameras take snapshots, so they are playfully called snappers.

clue.text: Hairstyle upset Kitty — Kitty's foremost fashionable style made over

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for kitty is turned upward

parts.note: the pot is the kitty of stakes in a card game

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of the word is taken
made over means the word for fashionable style is turned back

parts.note: the ton is fashion or high style

explanation.surface: Kitty is unhappy; her leading fashion style was given a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is an old word for fashion or the fashionable set.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is hair tied in a bun or tuft on top of the head.

clue.text: Relative of note embraced by successful student gaining qualification

indicators.note: the letter for note is held inside the word for successful student

parts.note: a grad is a graduate, one who has passed
MA is the Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A relative of some fame hugged by a graduate who earned her degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandma is an informal name for a grandmother, a family member.

clue.text: Gun company hogging attention

indicators.note: the word for company greedily holds the word for attention within it

parts.note: a firm is a business or company
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An arms company dominating the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearm is the general term for a weapon such as a pistol or rifle.

clue.text: A liqueur rejected after soft food — it's peppery

indicators.note: after means the reversed letters follow the word for soft food

parts.note: pap is bland soft food for infants

indicators.note: rejected means the A and the liqueur are thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A dinner guest sends back a liqueur after a bland baby-food course.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a spice ground from red peppers, so it is peppery by nature.

clue.text: Academic keeping old coin for display

indicators.note: the word for academic holds the letter for old inside it

parts.note: a prof is a professor

explanation.surface: A scholar holding on to an antique coin to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof coins are specially struck with polished dies for collectors, not for circulation.

clue.text: Girl's anger one initially ignored

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: initially ignored means the first letter of one is left out

explanation.surface: A girl's anger that one at first overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Composer drank endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for drank is removed

parts.note: to sup is to drink, so drank is supped

explanation.surface: A composer who drank without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of operettas and the Light Cavalry overture.

clue.text: Go downhill, trying to get tennis star's autograph?

definitions.meaning: to deteriorate, as a plant does when it bolts

definitions.text: trying to get tennis star's autograph?
definitions.meaning: a top tennis player is ranked as a seed, so an autograph hunter might dash toward one

explanation.walkthrough: In tennis the strongest players are 'seeded' so they avoid each other early in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed has stopped flowering, so the idiom means decline or decay.

clue.text: For example, no good reason not to translate T S Eliot

definitions.text: For example, no good reason not to

indicators.note: to translate is to render into another form, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An argument that there is no good reason to avoid translating the poet T S Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself an instance of the device: 'no good reason not to' means 'good reason to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, of which a double-negative phrase is an example.

clue.text: Material influence not about to be enveloped by cheers

indicators.note: the shortened word for influence is wrapped inside the word for cheers

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks or cheers

indicators.note: not means the letter for about is dropped from the word for influence

parts.note: to affect something is to influence it
C is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A fabric whose influence is about to be welcomed with cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' here is British slang for thanks, not a toast. 'not about' drops C, the circa abbreviation, from the word for influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric of silk or similar fibre, so it is a cloth.
